name: create_account
title: Create an account
description: Add an account to a plan. **This cannot be undone through this server**: YNAB's API has no endpoint that renames, closes or deletes an account, so a wrong name, a wrong type or a wrong opening balance can only be fixed by the user in the YNAB app. Confirm all three with the user before calling, and read the result back to them. Only six kinds of account can be created here; loan and debt accounts have to be added in the app.

plan_id.description: Id of the plan (YNAB's name for a budget) to act on. Omit it unless the user named a particular plan: the server then uses the plan it was configured with, falling back to the one most recently opened in YNAB. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_plans` rather than guessing it.

name.description: Name for the account as it will read in YNAB, e.g. "Chase Checking".

type.description: What kind of account this is. Only these six can be created through the API: `checking`, `savings`, `cash`, `creditCard`, `otherAsset`, `otherLiability`. The loan and debt types `list_accounts` reports — `mortgage`, `autoLoan` and the rest — cannot be created here and have to be added in the YNAB app.

balance.description: The balance the account starts with. Negative for money owed, which is how a credit card or a liability is opened. YNAB records it as the account's starting balance. A decimal amount in the plan's currency, never milliunits: pass 123.93 for $123.93, not 123930. At most three decimal places — anything finer is rejected rather than rounded, because silently altering a financial amount is worse than failing.

plan_id.description: Id of the plan this acted on, as the server resolved it. Check it against the plan the ids came from: with no `plan_id` and no configured default, the server acts on whichever plan was most recently opened in YNAB, which need not be the one a list tool was read from.

id.description: Account id, opaque. Pass it to the tools that take an account.

name.description: Account name as it appears in YNAB, e.g. "Chase Checking".

type.description: Kind of account: checking, savings, cash, creditCard, lineOfCredit, otherAsset, otherLiability, mortgage, autoLoan, studentLoan, personalLoan, medicalDebt or otherDebt. YNAB adds kinds without warning, so treat the list as open.

on_budget.description: Whether the account's money is part of the plan and can be assigned to categories. Tracking accounts (investments, a mortgage) are off budget.

closed.description: Whether the account is closed. Closed accounts are still listed.

note.description: Free-text note on the account, when it has one.

balance.description: Working balance in milliunits, where 1000 is one currency unit. Cleared plus uncleared.

balance_formatted.description: The working balance in the plan's currency format, e.g. "$1,234.56".

cleared_balance.description: Balance of cleared transactions only, in milliunits.

cleared_balance_formatted.description: The cleared balance in the plan's currency format.

uncleared_balance.description: Balance of uncleared transactions only, in milliunits.

uncleared_balance_formatted.description: The uncleared balance in the plan's currency format.

transfer_payee_id.description: The payee that stands for this account in a transfer: use it as the payee when moving money into this account. Null when YNAB reports none.

last_reconciled_at.description: When the account was last reconciled, ISO 8601. Absent if it never has been.

direct_import_linked.description: Whether YNAB imports this account's transactions from the bank automatically.

direct_import_in_error.description: Whether that bank connection has broken, in which case the balances may be stale.

account.description: The account as YNAB created it. Read it back to the user: this is the only chance to catch a wrong name or type while it is still cheap to talk about.

name: create_category
title: Create a category
description: Add a category to a plan, filed into an existing group. Setting `goal_target` gives the category a monthly target of that amount; adding `goal_target_date` makes it a target by that date instead. YNAB chooses the kind of target itself — there is no way to name one. A category cannot be hidden or deleted through the API once it exists, only renamed and re-filed, so creating one the user did not ask for leaves clutter only they can clear in the YNAB app.

plan_id.description: Id of the plan (YNAB's name for a budget) to act on. Omit it unless the user named a particular plan: the server then uses the plan it was configured with, falling back to the one most recently opened in YNAB. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_plans` rather than guessing it.

name.description: Name for the new category, as it will read in YNAB, e.g. "Vet".

category_group_id.description: The group to file the category under. It must already exist, and it cannot be one of YNAB's own internal groups. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_categories` rather than guessing it.

goal_target.description: Target amount for the category. A decimal amount in the plan's currency, never milliunits: pass 123.93 for $123.93, not 123930. At most three decimal places — anything finer is rejected rather than rounded, because silently altering a financial amount is worse than failing.

goal_target_date.description: Date the target should be met by, as 2026-12-01, which makes it a target-by-date rather than a monthly one. Omit it to leave any existing date alone.

goal_needs_whole_amount.description: Only meaningful on a "plan your spending" (NEED) target: `true` sets aside the target amount again each period, `false` refills the category up to it. YNAB ignores it on every other kind of target.

plan_id.description: Id of the plan this acted on, as the server resolved it. Check it against the plan the ids came from: with no `plan_id` and no configured default, the server acts on whichever plan was most recently opened in YNAB, which need not be the one a list tool was read from.

id.description: Category id, opaque. Pass it to the tools that take a category.

name.description: Category name as it appears in YNAB, e.g. "Groceries".

category_group_id.description: Id of the group this category sits in.

group_name.description: Name of the group this category sits in, e.g. "Immediate Obligations". Always present when the whole plan is listed, which is the only response that wraps a category in its group; when month or category_id narrows the call, only when YNAB itself names the group on the category.

group_hidden.description: Whether the group is hidden, which hides its categories in YNAB whatever their own `hidden` says. Present only when the whole plan is listed: no response narrowed by month or category_id carries the group itself.

hidden.description: Whether the category itself is hidden in YNAB. Hidden categories are still listed.

internal.description: True for YNAB's own built-in categories, of which "Ready to Assign" — money received but not yet assigned anywhere — is the one that matters. They are listed like any other category rather than filtered out.

note.description: Free-text note on the category, when it has one.

budgeted.description: Amount assigned to the category for the month, in milliunits, where 1000 is one currency unit.

budgeted_formatted.description: The assigned amount in the plan's currency format, e.g. "$1,234.56".

activity.description: Sum of the month's transactions in the category, in milliunits; spending is negative.

activity_formatted.description: The month's activity in the plan's currency format.

balance.description: Amount still available to spend in the category, in milliunits: what is assigned plus what rolled over, less the activity.

balance_formatted.description: The available balance in the plan's currency format.

goal_type.description: The kind of target set on the category, if any: TB (target balance), TBD (target balance by date), MF (monthly funding), NEED (plan your spending) or DEBT (debt payoff). Absent when the category has no target; YNAB adds kinds without warning.

goal_target_formatted.description: The target amount in the plan's currency format.

goal_target_date.description: Date the target is meant to be met, for the kinds of target that set one.

goal_percentage_complete.description: How far the target has been met, 0 to 100.

goal_under_funded.description: Still to assign this month to stay on track for the target, in milliunits. Zero when the category is on track.

goal_under_funded_formatted.description: The amount still to assign, in the plan's currency format.

category.description: The category as YNAB created it, with the target it worked out from the goal arguments. `group_name` and `group_hidden` are absent: a create response carries no group.

name: create_category_group
title: Create a category group
description: Add a category group — the heading categories sit under in YNAB. The group comes back empty; file categories into it with `create_category`, or move existing ones with `update_category`. A group cannot be hidden or deleted through the API, so creating one the user did not ask for leaves clutter only they can clear, in the app.

plan_id.description: Id of the plan (YNAB's name for a budget) to act on. Omit it unless the user named a particular plan: the server then uses the plan it was configured with, falling back to the one most recently opened in YNAB. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_plans` rather than guessing it.

name.description: Name for the new group, as it will read in YNAB. At most 50 characters.

plan_id.description: Id of the plan this acted on, as the server resolved it. Check it against the plan the ids came from: with no `plan_id` and no configured default, the server acts on whichever plan was most recently opened in YNAB, which need not be the one a list tool was read from.

id.description: Group id, opaque. Pass it as `category_group_id` to file a category.

name.description: Group name as it appears in YNAB, e.g. "Immediate Obligations".

hidden.description: Whether the group is hidden in YNAB, which hides every category in it whatever the category's own `hidden` says.

internal.description: True for YNAB's own built-in groups. A category cannot be filed into one.

category_group.description: The group as YNAB created it. Keep the id: groups have no listing endpoint of their own, and the only other way to find one is the `group_name` on a category in `list_categories`.

name: create_payee
title: Create a payee
description: Add a payee to a plan on its own. This is usually the wrong tool: `create_transaction` takes a `payee_name` and will match an existing payee or create one as it records the transaction, in a single request. Use this one only when the user wants the payee to exist before there is anything to record against it. YNAB does not say what happens if the name matches a payee that already exists, so check with `list_payees` first.

plan_id.description: Id of the plan (YNAB's name for a budget) to act on. Omit it unless the user named a particular plan: the server then uses the plan it was configured with, falling back to the one most recently opened in YNAB. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_plans` rather than guessing it.

name.description: Name for the new payee, as it will read in YNAB. At most 500 characters.

plan_id.description: Id of the plan this acted on, as the server resolved it. Check it against the plan the ids came from: with no `plan_id` and no configured default, the server acts on whichever plan was most recently opened in YNAB, which need not be the one a list tool was read from.

id.description: The payee's id, which every tool that filters on a payee wants.

name.description: The payee's name, as it reads in YNAB.

transfer_account_id.description: Set when this payee is the far side of a transfer: the id of the account money moves to. Null or absent on an ordinary payee.

payee.description: The payee as YNAB created it.

name: create_scheduled_transaction
title: Schedule a transaction
description: Set up a transaction YNAB will enter on a future date, optionally repeating. This records an intention rather than money that has moved: nothing appears in the account until the date arrives. Use `create_transaction` for something that already happened. YNAB documents no default for `frequency` and no meaning for individual values like `twiceAMonth`, so set it from what the user actually said.

plan_id.description: Id of the plan (YNAB's name for a budget) to act on. Omit it unless the user named a particular plan: the server then uses the plan it was configured with, falling back to the one most recently opened in YNAB. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_plans` rather than guessing it.

account_id.description: Account each occurrence will be entered in. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_accounts` rather than guessing it.

date.description: Date of the next occurrence. It must be in the future — a scheduled transaction is an instruction for something that has not happened yet — and no more than 5 years ahead. To record something that already happened, use `create_transaction`. An ISO date, written as 2026-08-14.

amount.description: Amount each occurrence will be entered for. A decimal amount in the plan's currency, never milliunits: pass 123.93 for $123.93, not 123930. At most three decimal places — anything finer is rejected rather than rounded, because silently altering a financial amount is worse than failing. Outflows are negative and inflows positive: -123.93 records spending 123.93, and 123.93 records receiving it.

payee_id.description: Payee each occurrence is recorded against. For a transfer, pass the other account's `transfer_payee_id` from `list_accounts` and leave `category_id` off. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_payees` rather than guessing it.

payee_name.description: Name of the payee, for when there is no `payee_id` to hand. YNAB matches it against an existing payee of the same name and creates one if there is none, so this can add a payee to the plan as a side effect. Ignored when `payee_id` is given, and capped at 200 characters.

category_id.description: Category each occurrence is assigned to. Leave it off for a transfer. A Credit Card Payment category is not permitted here, and `list_categories` returns those unfiltered, so check the group before picking one. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_categories` rather than guessing it.

memo.description: Note carried onto each occurrence. Free text, at most 500 characters.

flag_color.description: Colour of the flag on the transaction: `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue` or `purple`. Pass `null` or the empty string to clear a flag that is already there. Omit it to leave any existing flag alone.

frequency.description: How often the scheduled transaction repeats. `never` enters it once on its date and does not repeat. YNAB documents no default and no definition for the individual values, so set it from what the user said rather than inferring one.

subtransactions.description: Not supported, and present only to say so. YNAB has no way to express a scheduled transaction split across categories — no schema field, no endpoint — so passing this fails rather than quietly scheduling something with its lines dropped. Schedule one transaction per category, or record a split with `create_transaction` when it happens.

plan_id.description: Id of the plan this acted on, as the server resolved it. Check it against the plan the ids came from: with no `plan_id` and no configured default, the server acts on whichever plan was most recently opened in YNAB, which need not be the one a list tool was read from.

date_first.description: Date it was first scheduled for, as YYYY-MM-DD.

date_next.description: Date the next occurrence is due to be entered, as YYYY-MM-DD.

frequency.description: How often it repeats. One of "never", "daily", "weekly", "everyOtherWeek", "twiceAMonth", "every4Weeks", "monthly", "everyOtherMonth", "every3Months", "every4Months", "twiceAYear", "yearly", "everyOtherYear".

amount.description: The amount each occurrence will be entered for. In milliunits, where 1000 is one unit of the plan's currency, and outflows are negative.

memo.description: Note on the scheduled transaction, absent when it has none.

flag_name.description: The plan's own name for that flag colour, if it has one.

account_id.description: Id of the account each occurrence will be entered in.

payee_id.description: Id of the payee, absent when there is none.

category_id.description: Id of the category, absent when the transaction is uncategorised or a transfer.

category_name.description: Name of that category; a split transaction reports a placeholder name here.

transfer_account_id.description: Account this moves money to, when the transaction is a transfer rather than a spend.

deleted.description: True once the transaction has been deleted; YNAB keeps the record so clients sync.

scheduled_transaction_id.description: Id of the scheduled transaction this line belongs to.

amount.description: The line's share of the total. In milliunits, where 1000 is one unit of the plan's currency, and outflows are negative.

memo.description: Note on this line, absent when it has none.

payee_id.description: Id of this line's payee, absent when it has none.

category_id.description: Id of this line's category, absent when it is uncategorised.

transfer_account_id.description: Account this line moves money to, when the line is a transfer rather than a spend.

deleted.description: True once the line has been deleted; YNAB keeps the record so clients can sync.

subtransactions.description: The split lines, empty unless the transaction is split across categories.

scheduled_transaction.description: The scheduled transaction as YNAB created it, including the `date_next` it worked out.

name: create_transaction
title: Create transactions
description: Record one or more transactions in a plan. Always takes an array, so recording ten costs one request rather than ten; send at most 100 at a time and split a larger batch across calls. A transaction may be a simple spend, a transfer between accounts, or a split across several categories. Dates cannot be in the future. Setting `import_id` on a row marks it as imported, which makes YNAB match and overwrite a transaction the user entered by hand — leave it off for anything recorded on the user's behalf.

plan_id.description: Id of the plan (YNAB's name for a budget) to act on. Omit it unless the user named a particular plan: the server then uses the plan it was configured with, falling back to the one most recently opened in YNAB. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_plans` rather than guessing it.

account_id.description: Account the transaction is recorded in. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_accounts` rather than guessing it.

date.description: Date the transaction happened. It cannot be in the future: YNAB treats a future-dated transaction as a scheduled one and refuses it on this endpoint. An ISO date, written as 2026-08-14.

amount.description: Total amount of the transaction. A decimal amount in the plan's currency, never milliunits: pass 123.93 for $123.93, not 123930. At most three decimal places — anything finer is rejected rather than rounded, because silently altering a financial amount is worse than failing. Outflows are negative and inflows positive: -123.93 records spending 123.93, and 123.93 records receiving it.

payee_id.description: Payee the money went to or came from. To record a transfer, pass the other account's `transfer_payee_id` from `list_accounts` here and leave `category_id` off. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_payees` rather than guessing it.

payee_name.description: Name of the payee, for when there is no `payee_id` to hand. YNAB matches it against an existing payee of the same name and creates one if there is none, so this can add a payee to the plan as a side effect. Ignored when `payee_id` is given, and capped at 200 characters.

category_id.description: Category the transaction is assigned to. Leave it off for a transfer, and off when `subtransactions` is given — a split takes its categories from its lines. YNAB ignores a Credit Card Payment category here without saying so, and `list_categories` returns those unfiltered, so check the group before picking one. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_categories` rather than guessing it.

memo.description: Note on the transaction. Free text, at most 500 characters.

cleared.description: Whether the transaction has cleared the account: `uncleared` for one YNAB has not seen on a statement, `cleared` for one it has, `reconciled` for one locked against a reconciled balance. Reconciling is hard to undo in YNAB, so pass `reconciled` only when the user asked for it.

approved.description: Whether the transaction is already approved. Omit it and YNAB leaves the transaction unapproved, so it waits in the user's Approve queue for review; passing `true` skips that review entirely.

flag_color.description: Colour of the flag on the transaction: `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue` or `purple`. Pass `null` or the empty string to clear a flag that is already there. Omit it to leave any existing flag alone.

import_id.description: Your own id for this transaction, unique within its account, so that sending it twice creates it once. Setting it also tells YNAB the transaction was imported: YNAB then matches it against a transaction the user entered by hand on the same account for the same amount within ten days, and the imported amount wins. Omit it unless you are importing from a system that has its own ids — a transaction recorded on the user's behalf should be left user-entered. At most 36 characters.

amount.description: This line's share of the transaction. A decimal amount in the plan's currency, never milliunits: pass 123.93 for $123.93, not 123930. At most three decimal places — anything finer is rejected rather than rounded, because silently altering a financial amount is worse than failing. Outflows are negative and inflows positive: -123.93 records spending 123.93, and 123.93 records receiving it.

payee_id.description: Payee for this line, when it differs from the transaction's. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_payees` rather than guessing it.

payee_name.description: Name of the payee, for when there is no `payee_id` to hand. YNAB matches it against an existing payee of the same name and creates one if there is none, so this can add a payee to the plan as a side effect. Ignored when `payee_id` is given, and capped at 200 characters.

category_id.description: Category this line is assigned to. Ids are opaque strings YNAB assigns; get one from `list_categories` rather than guessing it.

memo.description: Note on this line. Free text, at most 500 characters.

subtransactions.description: Lines of a split transaction, each with its own amount and category. Omit for an ordinary transaction. A split cannot be edited afterwards — YNAB supports no way to add, change or remove a line once it exists — so get the lines right the first time.

transactions.description: The transactions to create. Pass one element to record a single transaction.

plan_id.description: Id of the plan this acted on, as the server resolved it. Check it against the plan the ids came from: with no `plan_id` and no configured default, the server acts on whichever plan was most recently opened in YNAB, which need not be the one a list tool was read from.

amount_formatted.description: `amount` in the plan's currency format, ready to show the user.

transfer_transaction_id.description: If a transfer, the transaction on the other side of it.

duplicate_import_ids.description: `import_id`s that were **not** created, because a transaction on the same account already carried them. Those rows were skipped and the rest were still created — this is a success reporting what was already recorded, not a failure to retry.

name: set_category_budget

description: Assign an amount to a category for a month — the everyday act of budgeting in YNAB.
